How strongly does the fitted deepSSF model select each part of the landscape at different
times of day, seasons and weather? Pick an hour, a season and a weather preset to see the
model's habitat-selection surface, and the log selection ratio of each landcover class.

- **What is mapped:** the habitat surface of the fitted model (the habitat head only, so
  every cell is treated as reachable), within 500 m of an observed fix. Brighter cells are
  more strongly selected. The colour scale is the same for every preset, so maps can be
  compared directly.
- **Weather presets:** real half-hours observed at the Oenpelli station in that season
  (same month), within an hour of the chosen time:
  - *cool & dry* and *hot & humid*: the 10th and 90th percentiles of wet bulb temperature,
    without rain;
  - *typical*: closest to the median of every weather variable;
  - *rain*: the median rain amount among half-hours with rain. There is none in the early
    dry season, and only some hours in the late dry season have it.
- **Bar chart:** the log selection ratio within the mask. 0 means the class is used in
  proportion to its availability; positive values mean it is selected for.

The maps are precomputed (347 scenarios). The methods, and partial dependence plots that
separate the effects of time and weather, are in the
[deepSSF Inference](deepssf_piggies_inference_landcover.ipynb) notebook. A local app that
recomputes maps for any time and weather is described in `apps/README.md`.
